courses.title: A Positive Approach to Language Teaching (GS)
courses.description: Kommentar: This seminar introduces Positive Language Pedagogy, a strength-based approach to language teaching inspired by Positive Psychology and child-centered didactics. Participants will explore how concepts such as the PERMA model (Positive Emotions, Engagement, Relationships, Meaning, and Accomplishment), growth mindset, and appreciative classroom interaction can support young learners’ emotional well-being, motivation, and language development. The course focuses on playful, age-appropriate activities and routines that help create a warm, encouraging learning environment in the primary English classroom. In addition to supporting pupils, the seminar also highlights the importance of teacher well-being as a foundation for sustainable and joyful teaching. Through a mix of theory, hands-on practice, and reflection, students will develop ideas for implementing positive language education in everyday classroom life. Reading recommendation: Students are encouraged to read the Happy Learning resource book (Sambanis/Ludwig 2024, Hueber-Verlag) before or during the seminar. The book offers a practical introduction to key concepts of Positive Pedagogy and will be referenced regularly throughout the course. Reading it will support your understanding of the theoretical foundations and provide hands-on ideas for implementing positive practices in the English classroom. Schließen

courses.title: Current Developments in Primary Teaching and Learning (GS)
courses.description: Kommentar: What are the questions that you still have in connection with teaching English in primary school? How to stick to English and when to allow the use of German or really any resource that learners bring to the classroom? How much writing to integrate and how to develop their competences in this respect? Or how to develop these equally important aspects, which are not that easy to test, such as values and competences in relation to cultural aspects, literary learning, multiliteracies or learners’ autonomy? In this course, we will take your own questions as well as aspects, which are currently widely discussed, as a starting point and will, in this way, explore current developments in teaching English at primary level. The course will start with a short international exchange with a course at a Swedish university, in which you explore aspects as the ones enumerated above. The course will also require you to become active and will include a microteaching session, which you will jointly plan and carry out within the course. Parts of this course will be taught online. Dates for on-site and online sessions will be announced in class. The first two sessions will be on-site. Literature will be provided in the course via Moodle/Learn@FU. Schließen

courses.title: Entwicklung, Forschung und Evaluation. Variante 1: ohne Vorbereitung MA-Arbeit (GS/ISS/GYM)
courses.description: Kommentar: The focus of this seminar is the professional activity of teaching English as a foreign language (EFL), considered both theoretically (as an object of investigation) and practically (as it is realized in the classroom). From the perspective of Performative Didactics, the course covers selected issues in teaching English as a foreign language (the arts in language teaching, digital texts, multilingualism, creativity in the classroom, etc.). Performative Didactics is defined as an approach that emphasizes embodied learning and draws on techniques and processes from the performing arts, amongst others from theater. Students get the possibility to discover activities for the EFL classroom inspired by Performative Didactics as well as Positive Psychology (focusing on strengths & flourishing as well as on student & teacher wellbeing). The course gives insight into relevant studies (didactic & neuroscientific findings), and other scholarly publications. These will be critically discussed by the participants together with the lecturer, and linked to theoretical foundations, to the current body of knowledge, and to practical considerations/teaching ideas. Students are expected to attend class regularly and to participate actively, which includes a presentation ("Referat (ca. 10 Minuten) mit Ausarbeitung (ca. 5 Seiten)"). Focus areas: Performative Didactics, research from didactics, neuroscience and other sister disciplines, Positive Psychology, teaching ideas. Recommended readings: Sambanis, M. & Ludwig, C. (2024): Happy Learning – Glücklich und erfolgreich Sprachen lernen . München: Hueber. Sambanis, M. & Walter, M. (2022): Make it work! Interaktive Impulse zum Sprachenlernen. Von neuesten Befunden der Neurowissenschaft zu konkreten Unterrichtsimpulsen . Berlin: Cornelsen (Reihe Neurowissenschaftliche Impulse). Course structure: Lectures, seminars, teaching activities, group work, performative components, presentations plus feedback, and discussions. Schließen

courses.title: Places and Non-Places
courses.description: Kommentar: Topic: Towards the end of postmodernism – and at the dawn of the "internet age" – the French anthropologist Marc Augé developed a conceptual model to describe the rather vague feeling of arbitrariness and interchangeability of space we experience in modern cities, the idea that the few identifiable "places" in our contemporary urban environments are mere remnants of earlier, culturally inscribed sites, re-manufactured for commercial (touristic) purposes. The vast remaining areas of the city are, according to Augé, "non-places" and urban "filaments" that do not provide a sense of belonging. This observation frees city dwellers to (artistically or otherwise) occupy, misappropriate or re-inscribe objects of the urban fabric. In the early 1990s, the term hypermodernism (or supermodernism) was introduced to provide a framework for these observations in fields ranging from philosophy to anthropology and architecture. Program: We will consider this concept and its more recent iterations with respect to places of infrastructure (train stations, airports), shopping centers, so-called POPS (privately owned public spaces) and urban wilderness areas, as well as new and planned buildings in Berlin (by international architecture firms such as OMA and Herzog & de Meuron). Course participants will be encouraged to explore the city on their own and "respond" to particular sites through visuals, audio recordings, (creative) texts and other forms of artistic expression. Can I take this course? Yes, if you are interested in urbanism, architecture, and related fields; willing to read some theoretical texts; eager to explore the city on your own; open to (artistic) experimentation. The course has no further prerequisites. Requirements and Grading: There will be assigned readings of ten to thirty pages per week. To earn five ECTS credits, you will have to attend the first meeting on October 13, 2026, plus at least twelve further sessions. Regular and active participation in class discussions is required, as well as participation in a group student presentation. You will need to pass a final exam on the last day of the course (February 8, 2027). Schließen

courses.title: Public History als Geschichtskultur I
courses.description:
Kommentar: Das Modul kombiniert in zwei Semestern theoretische, praktische und empirische Zugänge zu Public History als Geschichtskultur. In diesem Seminar im WS 2026/27 werden theoretische Grundlagen erarbeitet, mit denen sich gesellschaftliche Verhandlungen von Geschichte und konkrete Produkte der Public History analysieren lassen. Dies beinhaltet grundlegende Konzepte der Geschichtsdidaktik (z.B. Geschichtsbewusstsein, Geschichtskultur, Erinnerungskultur, Narrativität, Authentizität), Konzepte zur Analyse von Geschichte im gesellschaftspolitischen Kontext (z.B. Diversität, Race/Class/Gender als Kategorien sozialer Ungleichheit, postkoloniale Konzepte), sowie eine Auseinandersetzung mit modernen Medienumgebungen, in denen Geschichte in unserer Gegenwart präsentiert wird. Auf Grundlage der theoretischen Konzepte analysieren wir beispielhaft relevante Felder der öffentlichen Geschichte wie Gedenkstätten und Museen, mediale Darstellungen von Geschichte oder Living History. Im zweiten Teil des Moduls im Sommersemester 2027 wird die Erarbeitung und Reflexion eines eigenen Public History Projekts im Mittelpunkt des Seminars stehen. Schließen

Literaturhinweise: • Martin Lücke / Irmgard Zündorf: Einführung in die Public History (Reihe «UTB Einführungen» Bd. 4909), Göttingen: Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht 2018; • Astrid Erll: Kollektives Gedächtnis und Erinnerungskulturen. Eine Einführung, Berlin: J.B. Metzler 2017; • Christine Gundermann u.a.: Schlüsselbegriffe der Public History, Göttingen: Vandenhoeck & Rupprecht 2021. Schließen

courses.title: Arbeits- und Analysefelder der Public History
courses.description:
Kommentar: Public History umfasst die Arbeit in Museen und Gedenkstätten sowie in politischen Stiftungen, privaten Vereinen, wirtschaftlichen Unternehmen oder öffentlichen Medieninstitutionen. Im Seminar gehen wir auf die Arbeitsfelder in den genannten Bereichen ein und auf die dortigen Möglichkeiten der Präsentation von Geschichte. Darüber werden wir mit Referent:innen aus den verschiedenen Arbeitsbereichen diskutieren und erste Analyseansätze für die Auseinandersetzung mit den Geschichtspräsentationen entwickeln. Das Ziel der Lehrveranstaltung liegt einerseits darin einen breiten Überblick über mögliche Arbeitsfelder für Public Historians zu bekommen und andererseits Einblicke in die Produktion verschiedener Geschichtspräsentationen zu erhalten. Zudem werden anhand einiger Beispiele praktische Grenzen der Public History diskutiert. Dafür werden geschichtspolitische, mediale und wirtschaftliche Aspekte einzelner „Produkte“ herausgegriffen. Schließen

Literaturhinweise: Hilmar Sack: Geschichte im politischen Raum. Theorie – Praxis – Berufsfelder, Tübingen 2016; Thomas Fischer/Thomas Schuhbauer: Geschichte in Film und Fernsehen. Theorie – Praxis – Berufsfelder, Tübingen 2016, Thomas Thiemeyer: Geschichte im Museum. Theorie – Praxis – Berufsfelder, Tübingen 2018; Habbo Knoch: Geschichte in Gedenkstätten. Theorie – Praxis – Berufsfelder, Tübingen 2020; Martin Lücke/Irmgard Zündorf: Einführung in die Public History, Göttingen 2018. Schließen

Kommentar: Die mehrteilige Veranstaltung ist eine Kooperationsveranstaltung mit der Ständigen Konferenz der NS-Gedenkorte im Berliner Raum (StäKo). Die Teilnehmenden besuchen in dieser Veranstaltung sechs verschiedene Gedenkorte und ihre Ausstellungen. courses.description:
Hinweise für Studierende: Sie müssen die LV 17208 sowie das passende Seminar „Sprachbildung“ buchen – beachten Sie hierzu bitte folgende Hinweise: https://www.geisteswissenschaften.fu-berlin.de/we04/didaktik/daz/studium/ma-praxissemester/index.html Schließen

Kommentar: Das Seminar findet in Kooperation mit der Maria-Leo-Grundschule statt. Sie entwickeln sprachsensible Unterrichtsmaterialien für das Schulprojekt „Warum Unterschiedlichkeit die Welt verändert!“ – für eine heterogene Gruppe von DaZ-Schüler*innen (Kl. 4–6). Nach einer Einführung in die Erwerbsprogression des Deutschen als Zweitsprache lernen Sie das pädagogische Konzept, die Arbeitsweise und das geplante Projekt der Maria-Leo-Grundschule durch Vertreter*innen der Schule sowie die Schule selbst kennen. Aufbauend darauf analysieren und überarbeiten Sie vorhandene Materialien, ergänzen sie bei Bedarf mit differenzierenden Angeboten (Schwerpunkt Wortschatz) und erstellen umsetzbare Entwürfe. Die Entwürfe werden gemeinsam mit der Schule zwischenevaluiert, anschließend ggf. überarbeitet und schließlich im Unterricht erprobt. Anhand der Erfahrungen von Schüler*innen, Studierenden und Lehrkräften wird die Erprobung gemeinsam reflektiert. Das Seminar bietet Ihnen also die Möglichkeit, praxisnahe Erfahrungen in der Entwicklung sprachsensibler Materialen zu sammeln und Ihre Kompetenzen im Bereich Deutsch als Zweitsprache zu stärken. Melden Sie sich bitte nur, wenn Sie echtes Interesse an diesem Schwerpunkt haben und nicht allein, weil die Uhrzeit passt, da uns die erfolgreiche Zusammenarbeit mit der Kooperationsschule am Herzen liegt. Schließen

courses.title: Colloquium zur Zeitgeschichte
courses.description: Kommentar: Im Colloquium zur Zeitgeschichte werden laufende Forschungsarbeiten vor allem zur Geschichte des 20. Jahrhunderts vorgestellt und diskutiert, Dissertationen im Arbeitsbereich ebenso wie Projekte auswärtiger Gäste. Den Masterstudierenden wird so ein Zugang zur „Forschung als Prozess“ geboten, wie das Modul durchaus treffend heißt. Sie erhalten Einblick in die Weite der Themen und Zugänge im Fach, damit auch Anregungen für eigenes Arbeiten, und lernen, sich (mit eigenen Fragen!) auch zu Themen zu verhalten, in denen sie sich bisher noch nicht auskannten. In eigenen, „internen“ Sitzungen mit den Masterstudierenden wird das besprochen und begleitet. Nach Absprache besteht hier auch die Möglichkeit, Ideen zur eigenen Masterarbeit, ein Exposé, einen Kapitelentwurf o.ä. zu präsentieren. Schließen

courses.title: The Arabian Peninsula and the Persian Gulf from the 19th to the 21st centuries at the crossroads of local, imperial and global interests
courses.description: Kommentar: While the Arabian Peninsula and the Persian (or: Arab) Gulf have long been at the crossroads of international trade, from the Incense Road to early trade in pearls, and while early modern empires, including the Portuguese, attempted to control the routes through the Gulf and Red Sea, imperial rivalry culminated in the late 19th century with the expansion of the East India Company and the Ottoman Empire as well as German attempts to expand influence to the Gulf through an expansion of the Baghdad-railway to the Gulf. The discovery of oil in southern Iran on the eve of World War I and the shift from coal to oil and gas as major fuels in the 20th century sparked new international competition which coincided with the establishment of nation-states. On the Arabian coast of the Gulf, these increasingly compete by trying to establish themselves as global hubs of transport, financial infrastructure and industry, as well as tourist destinations, beyond the export of petrochemicals. Beyond geo-politics and economics, which dominate the current debate about the region, the course will also address selected topics such as international migration, (neoliberal) urbanisation, nation-branding and models of governance. This course has a threefold aim: to provide an understanding of the history of the region and selected major current themes from a global history perspective, to explore the historiography and approaches to Gulf history, and to acquaint participants with a variety of sources available to study the region. Schließen

courses.title: Research Colloquium: 25 Years of Global War on Terror
courses.description: Kommentar: Taking the 25th anniversary of the Global War on Terror (GWOT) as its point of departure, this seminar offers a critical examination of the political, legal, social, and cultural consequences of one of the most influential security paradigms of the 21st century. Particular attention will be paid to the processes of securitization set in motion by the GWOT and their implications for Islamic movements and Muslim communities in Europe. The seminar asks how global security discourses have shaped local realities, while focusing on the intersections of counterterrorism policies, public debates, and everyday experiences. By connecting global and local dynamics, we analyze the ways in which security practices have transformed state–society relations, notions of citizenship, and the public visibility of Islam in European contexts. The seminar will also feature guest lectures by leading scholars whose research has significantly shaped the field of study. Schließen

Kommentar: Das Stress Free Pets Zertifizierungsprogramm für Tierärzte vermittelt Fähigkeiten und Wissen, um einen möglichst stress- und angstfreien Umgang mit Patienten in der Kleintierpraxis zu ermöglichen - Körpersprache von Hunden verstehen - Körpersprache von Katzen verstehen - Kooperatives Lernen: Theorie und Training für das klinische Umfeld - Wie man in der Klinik eine stressfreie Umgebung erzeugt - Stress, Furcht und Angst im klinischen Umfeld erkennen und reduzieren - Einführung in "Stress Free" Umgangstechniken - Umgang mit unseren Hundepatienten - Umgang mit unseren Katzenpatienten - Stress, Furcht und Angst schon vor Ankunft in der Klinik reduzieren - Hilfreiche Medikamente zur Stressreduktion - Umsetzung und Fortführung des "Stress Free" Programms Schließen

courses.description:
Hinweise für Studierende: 1. Semesterhälfte

Kommentar: Dieser Wahlpflichtkurs vermittelt grundlegende Fähigkeiten und theoretisches Wissen, um moderne Methoden der Künstlichen Intelligenz (KI) in der Verhaltensforschung (Computational Ethology) effektiv einzusetzen. - Grundlagen der klassischen und computergestützten Verhaltensforschung - Einführung in KI-gestützte Sensordaten-, Bild- und Videoverarbeitung zur automatisierten Verhaltenserkennung - Praxisprojekt: Durchführung eines ersten kleinen Projekts anhand strukturierter Anleitungen - Eigenständige Entwicklung, Anpassung und Validierung computergestützter Analysemethoden - Ethische Implikationen: Diskussion über Datenschutz, Bias und den Einfluss digitaler Überwachung auf das Tierwohl Schließen

courses.title: Post- and Decolonial Approaches to Islam in Europe
courses.description: Kommentar: What does decolonial knowledge production mean? How does it converge with or differ from postcolonial theory? How can decolonial perspectives be used to challenge and further develop established knowledge orders? Which approaches does research on Islam offer in this regard and what are its institutional limitations? What fields of practice do decolonial approaches open up within and beyond the university? In this seminar, we will explore these questions. We will pay particular attention to the field of research on Islam in Europe. We will examine approaches to decolonial theory and occasionally engage in conversations with scholars and initiatives relevant to this field. Schließen

courses.title: Political Islam: Ideological Trends and Social Movements
courses.description: Kommentar: The scholarship on political Islam has explained its ideas largely through the forces that surround them. Islamist thought has been read as a reaction to the modern state, as a symptom of colonial rupture and failed development, as an effect of the secular power that reshapes religion into an object it can govern. Each of these accounts illuminates something real about the conditions under which political Islam arose. What they leave in shadow is the level at which its thinkers were themselves at work: the level of concepts, where a figure like Qutb or Khomeini was not simply responding to modern power but arguing, from within an inherited tradition, over what its central concepts should now mean. This seminar reads modern Islamist thought at that level. Its analytical framework is a specific reading of the approach of Conceptual History. A political concept is treated here as a site of contest whose meaning is fixed by the situation of the one who wields it, and whose successive redefinitions register the deeper transformation of the tradition that carries it. The concepts at the center of the seminar—Islamic government, the Islamic state, Islamic politics, and those clustered around them—have exactly this kind of history. They carried a settled weight for as long as the institutions and authorities of the pre-modern order held; when that order gave way before the modern state and politics, their sense came loose, and each thinker was left to fix it anew. The ideological trends and social movements of the past century took shape around these rival fixings. The seminar opens by setting out this approach, then turns to a close reading of the founding texts of modern Islamism: the treatises and essays in which leading figures set out, in their own words, what an Islamic political order demands. The reading is organized around the shared cluster of concepts and pursued across both the Sunni and the Shi?i worlds, whose thinkers drew on one inheritance and worked it from different situations. On the Sunni side, the seminar takes up Hasan al-Banna, Sayyid Qutb, Abu al-A?la Mawdudi, and Taqi al-Din al-Nabhani; on the Shi?i side, Ruhollah Khomeini, Morteza Motahhari, Muhammad Baqir al-Sadr, and Ali Shariati—figures whose writings founded the major Islamist movements of the twentieth century or gave them their decisive intellectual form. Set against one another at the level of these concepts and their meanings, their texts reveal how a common inheritance was configured into competing, and often opposed, visions of Islamic politics. After introducing this analytical approach, students will work directly with the primary texts, acquire the means to read political and religious concepts as historical formations with a career of their own, and come to see the divided field of modern political Islam as a single sustained argument over how Islam and political authority belong together. Schließen

courses.title: writing the middle east: reader-focussed texts
courses.description:
Hinweise für Studierende: follow the course here: https://nodiscipline.hypotheses.org/ (not in moodle); see the course schedule on the blog

Kommentar: This is not your standard academic writing course. Forget the five-paragraph essay and the "state your thesis in the introduction" drill — here, we're interested in writing that actually does something for a reader. Building on the texts you're reading in Studying the Middle East, you'll pick one or two that get under your skin — texts you want to push back on, extend, or pick apart — and turn that engagement into a 5,000-word response essay. But the real work of this course is learning how to write it well. We'll draw heavily on reader-centered approaches to academic writing: instead of asking "what do I want to say" and instead of writing as if being examined, you'll learn to ask "what does my reader need, and why should they care." It's a shift that changes everything — how you open a piece, how you build an argument, even what counts as a good sentence. Expect less "correct academic style" and more: what makes writing worth reading. Schließen

courses.title: data empire: how information built and broke civilizations
courses.description:
Hinweise für Studierende: follow the course here: https://nodiscipline.hypotheses.org/ (not in moodle); see the course schedule on the blog

Kommentar: Long before satellites and algorithms, humans were already counting, categorizing, and recording each other — and every act of counting has always been an act of power. This seminar reads Roopika Risam’s Data Empire as its spine, tracing an 11,000-year history of data from Ice Age tally marks to AI-driven surveillance states, and asks a deceptively simple question: who decides what gets counted, and who benefits? Each session pairs one phase of Risam’s history with a different disciplinary lens — anthropology, law, economics, computer science, media studies — to interrogate how recordkeeping has organized empires, justified conquest, valued human lives, and now trains the algorithms shaping our own. Students bring their own regional and disciplinary interests to bear on a genuinely global story, discovering that the politics of data are never just technical. No prior background in data science, computing, or quantitative methods is required. Schließen

courses.title: reading happiness and the middle east
courses.description:
Hinweise für Studierende: follow the course here: https://nodiscipline.hypotheses.org/ (not in moodle); see the course schedule on the blog

Kommentar: Is happiness a private feeling or a public demand — and who decides what counts as a happy life, a happy family, a happy nation? This seminar reads Sara Ahmed's The Promise of Happiness across the semester as its core text, using her critique of happiness as a social and political technology to interrogate discourses of happiness, contentment, and national well-being in Middle Eastern contexts — from state happiness indices and ministries of happiness to gendered expectations, migration and melancholia, and youth movements' claims to joy as resistance. Each session works through one strand of Ahmed's argument and tests it against a regional case, building toward a final essay in which students apply and critique her framework on a Middle Eastern happiness discourse of their choosing. No prior background in affect theory is required. Schließen

courses.title: (S) Einführung in die wissenschaftliche Literatur der Semitistik und Arabistik
courses.description: Kommentar: Qualifikationsziele: Die Studentinnen und Studenten erwerben aufbauende Kompetenzen in exemplarischen Themenfeldern in den Bereichen der Schriftkulturen, oralen Literaturen und der Primärquellen der in den Schwerpunktbereichen behandelten Gesellschaften des Vorderen Orients. Sie erweitern ihre Kompetenzen über die wichtigsten fachspezifischen Rechercheverfahren. Die Studentinnen und Studenten können die historische Entwicklung einzelner Literaturen des Vorderen Orients in einen übergeordneten literaturwissenschaftlichen und regionalen Kontext einordnen. Dabei sind sie in der Lage, Quellen, Literaturen und normative bzw. grundlegende Texte in Beziehung zur Stellung ethnischer und religiöser Minderheiten, Genderfragen zu setzen und diese zu kontextualisieren. Sie können Kenntnisse über Beziehungen und gegenseitige Verflechtungen von Literaturen des Vorderen Orients auf die Bereiche Kultur, Religion und Ideengeschichte anwenden. Inhalte: Das Studium vermittelt einen Überblick über die wichtigsten arabischsprachigen, iranischsprachigen und türksprachigen Schriftzeugnisse, Quellengruppen und Literaturen, welche die Grundlage für das wissenschaftliche Arbeiten in den betreffenden Schwerpunktbereichen bilden. Es wird der Stoff anhand exemplarischer Beispiele aus einzelnen literarischen Epochen oder Textgattungen aus der Sicht des gewählten Schwerpunktbereichs vertieft. Schließen

courses.title: Festmahl der Worte – Essen in der arabischen Literatur und Kultur
courses.description:
Kommentar: In dieser Lehrveranstaltung widmen wir uns dem reichen Erbe des sozialen Essens und Trinkens in der arabischen Welt der Vormoderne. Wie wurden Festmähler und Trinkgelage nicht nur als kulinarische, sondern auch als soziale, politische und literarische Phänomene inszeniert? Welche Rolle spielen die Sinne? Wir erkunden, welche Rolle Großzügigkeit und Geiz in der arabischen Gesellschaft spielten, welche Gerichte und Getränke serviert wurden und wie sie zubereitet und angerichtet wurden. Ein besonderer Fokus liegt auf der literarischen Darstellung in Adab-Literatur, Dichtung und Kochbüchern. Die Veranstaltung verbindet historische, literarische und kulturelle Perspektiven und lädt dazu ein, die Vielfalt und Bedeutung des Genießens in der arabischen Welt neu zu entdecken. Im Zentrum des Seminars stehen Forschungsliteratur zur historischen Kontextualisierung der Texte und sowie zur historischen Anthropologie der Sinne. Schließen

courses.title: Liebende, Gazellen, Dichter und Wüstenwinde – Stimmen aus der klassischen arabischen Literatur
courses.description: Kommentar: In dieser Lehrveranstaltung lesen und analysieren die Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmer eine Auswahl poetischer Texte verschiedener Autoren aus der klassischen arabischen Literatur. Die behandelten Werke stammen aus der vorislamischen Zeit bis in die umayyadische Epoche und vermitteln einen Einblick in die Entwicklung der arabischen Dichtung von ihren frühen Anfängen bis zu ihren ersten Blütezeiten im Islam. Anhand der Lektüre ausgewählter Gedichte lernen die Studierenden zentrale Themen, Motive und Ausdrucksformen der klassischen arabischen Poesie kennen und gewinnen einen ersten Zugang zu ihrer literarischen und kulturgeschichtlichen Bedeutung. courses.title: Sprache, Kultur und Grammatik: Eine Reise durch die arabische Welt
courses.description: Kommentar: Dieser Kurs verbindet den systematischen Erwerb grammatischer Strukturen mit der Auseinandersetzung mit kulturellen, gesellschaftlichen und historischen Themen der arabischen Welt. Anhand vielfältiger authentischer und didaktisch aufbereiteter Texte beschäftigen sich die Teilnehmenden mit Literatur, Kunst, Musik, Geschichte, Traditionen, aktuellen Entwicklungen und dem Alltagsleben in verschiedenen arabischen Ländern. Ergänzt wird die Textarbeit durch die Analyse ausgewählter Videos, Dokumentationen und multimedialer Materialien, die unterschiedliche Perspektiven auf die arabische Kultur vermitteln. Die Grammatik wird dabei nicht isoliert, sondern in konkreten Kommunikationssituationen und kulturellen Kontexten erarbeitet und angewendet. Ziel des Kurses ist es, die sprachliche Kompetenz zu erweitern, das Textverständnis zu vertiefen und gleichzeitig ein differenziertes Verständnis der kulturellen Vielfalt der arabischen Welt zu entwickeln. German Literature in Translation: Berlin Alexanderplatz
courses.description: Kommentar: Topic: Alfred Döblin's Berlin Alexanderplatz, published in 1929, is the best-known big-city novel in the German language, a work of literary modernism frequently compared with James Joyce's Ulysses (1922) and John Dos Passos' Manhattan Transfer (1925). The plot, which is told in nine 'books', revolves around the former construction worker Franz Biberkopf, who is released from prison into the bustling streets of Weimar-era Berlin. Despite his best intentions he gets pulled into a life of crime and betrayal. The narrative technique of the novel, groundbreaking in its time, is fast-paced and experimental, montage-passages capture a cacophony of urban voices and disembodied discourses (politics, popular culture, advertising) of the so-called Golden Twenties. The chaotic, brutal, sexually permissive metropolis becomes a central character shaping Franz’s fate as much as his own choices. The novel presents a powerful portrait of urban life, moral collapse, and survival in a society on the brink of catastrophe. Program: The course offers an intensive reading experience and lively seminar discussions. We will read the novel at the good clip of about fifty pages per week and discuss its features and its literary, cultural, and political context. The reference text will be Michael Hofmann's English translation of the novel (Penguin Classics 2018), but students may read the text in any language. The course is designed to be entirely device-free: no smart phones, laptops, tablets etc. in class. Can I take this course? Yes, if you are interested in literature and willing to commit to reading, carefully and closely, a demanding novel at the pace of about fifty pages per week. The course is open to all Erasmus+ students. Requirements: To earn 5 ECTS credits, students are required to attend the first meeting on October 14, 2026, plus at least twelve of the remaining weekly meetings. Successful seminar participants will carefully read the assigned chapters, participate actively in class discussion, lead a seminar discussion, and pass a final exam. By the second meeting on October 21, all students will have purchased their personal copies of the novel. Schließen

courses.title: Artificial Humans, Robots and Androids in Film and Literature
courses.description: Kommentar: Topic: Narratives about the creation of artificial humans go back thousands of years. Among the more well-known examples are the story of Pygmalion in Ovid’s Metamorphoses whose sculpture of a woman was so beautiful that he fell in love with it and made it come to life, and Frankenstein, the scientist in Mary Shelley’s novel who creates a giant man from parts of dead bodies. Some narratives of this kind serve as a warning against human hubris by showing that these creatures become perilously uncontrollable, such as in Frankenstein and in Jewish legends around the Golem, a humanoid figure made from clay. Since the 20th century, androids and robots in fiction may not be concerned with hubris anymore, but still pose existential questions about what it means to be human and whether there should be limits to technological progress. One of the central topics is whether these robots or androids which are made to serve humans, but are frequently superior in physical strength and intellectual prowess, will remain slaves or try to become the masters themselves. Program: We will take a look at the evolution of narratives about creating artificial humans (the Golem, Frankenstein, Homunculus), study literary texts that explore the relationship of humans and artificially created humanoids (Karel Capek Rossum’s Universal Robots, Isaac Asimov’s I, Robot and Ian McEwan’s Machines Like Me), and examine well-known Science Fiction films that depict humanoid robots and/ or androids (clips from Fritz Lang’s Metropolis, Ridley Scott’s Blade Runner, Alex MacGarland’s Ex Machina, and James Cameron’s The Terminator). In doing so, we will examine how fiction reflects real-world technological developments, human fears and desires, as well as gender roles and society’s relationship with technology more generally. Is this the right course for you? The course is open to students from all fields, from the sciences as well as from the humanities. However, you should be able to read English texts at a high level, be prepared to study a variety of academic as well as literary texts and be interested in the topic as well as in in-depth analysis of texts and films. You should also be prepared to either attend the 4 film screenings (right after the course, Thursdays, 6-8 p.m., in December and January) or watch the films on streaming platforms where you may have to pay ca. 3-4 Euros per film. Workload and Assessment: To obtain 5 ECTS credits, you will have to study and engage with the course materials (an average of 15-20 pages of academic and/ or literary texts per week), pass a mid-term test before Christmas and sit a written exam at the end of the semester. If you want to participate, you must attend the first, at the latest the second session. Students must attend at least 85% of the classes (14 out of 16). Some of the materials will be available in digital form on Blackboard; additionally, students have to purchase the reader (a collection of photocopied texts in printed form) from the copy shop at Königin-Luise-Str. 39, near U-Bahnhof Dahlem Dorf. Schließen

courses.title: Literary and Philosophical Responses to Existential Risk
courses.description: Kommentar: Topic: Are we doomed? What does the realization that the very survival of humanity is in doubt mean for contemporary debates in science, culture, politics and population ethics? While the risk of human extinction from natural causes (e.g. an asteroid impact) has been a major topic of literature and popular culture for a long time, contemporary debates focus primarily on anthropogenic threats such as nuclear disaster, climate change, and misaligned Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). Effective altruists and longtermists argue that humanity is currently passing through a 'great filter' of existential risk and will reap unimaginable, even astronomical benefits if it succeeds. Natalists worry about population decline, while anti-natalists and eco-fascists consider the suffering of humans and farm animals to be so vast that human extinction should be allowed or even hastened. Program: The course will be conducted as an interdisciplinary seminar, with student-led discussions of major works in the emerging field of Existential Risk Studies. We will survey the literature in roughly chronological order, discuss several works of dystopian fiction and film and delve into the political and ethical debates surrounding the threat of human extinction. Can I take this course? The course is open to students from all fields and has no further prerequisites. You should be able to debate complex ideas and read, without difficulty, English texts aimed at an educated general audience. Requirements: There will be assigned readings of ten to thirty pages per week, plus one book report per student. Depending on your topic, you may need to purchase a book. In addition, you will watch (and possibly purchase/rent) approximately three feature movies on your own. To earn five ECTS credits, you will have to attend the first meeting on October 13, 2026, plus at least twelve further sessions. Regular and active participation in class discussions is required. You will need to pass a final exam on the last day of the course (February 8, 2027). Schließen

courses.title: Krabat auf TikTok. Gegenwärtige Adaptionsprozesse für Kinder- und Jugendmedien
courses.description: Kommentar: Dieses literaturtheoretisch angelegte Seminar greift ein Desiderat der Kinder- und Jugendliteraturforschung auf: Das Feld der Adaptionen, verstanden als Medienwechsel, der ein kinder- bzw. jugendliterarisches Artefakt verwendet und neu darstellt. Zwar sind Literaturverfilmungen oder Hörspieladaptionen seit geraumer Zeit in schulischen und universitären Curricula angekommen und allgegenwärtig. Neue Tendenzen werden dagegen bislang kaum beforscht, deren Prozessen eine jeweils ganz spezifische Ästhetik zu eigen ist, die sich am konkreten Medienwechsel analysieren lässt. Folgende Adaptionsprozesse werden u.a. untersucht: vom Drama zum Roman („Himmelwärts“), von Hip Hop („Fettes Brot“) zum Comic, vom Kinderbuch „Krabat“ zum Gothic Rock-Album der Band ASP („Zaubererbrüder“) sowie die Darstellung von Kinderliteratur als Freizeitparkattraktion, Kreuzfahrtreise oder TikTok. Sie müssen somit die Bereitschaft mitbringen, sich theoretisch in das Feld der Adaptionsforschung einzuarbeiten und neue Forschungsbereiche eigenständig, aber natürlich im Seminar begleitet zu erarbeiten. Die folgende Literatur muss vor Seminarbeginn angeschafft werden, weitere Seminarlektüre wird noch bekannt gegeben: Gunther Buskies, Jonas Engelmann (Hg.): Schwule Mädchen Sondereinheit. 10 Fettes Brot Songcomics Karen Köhler: Himmelwärts Otfried Preußler: Krabat Schließen

courses.title: Basic Income and Inequality
courses.description: Kommentar: Subject: In 2021 the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW) began paying 122 people €1,200 a month, tax free, no strings attached, for three years. The study, known as the Basic Income Pilot Project, aimed to contribute empirical evidence to the debate over the merits of a basic income. The first results of the experiment were released in April 2025. Program: We will approach the study of a basic income through the literature on income inequality and its social implications when present at levels observed in Germany today. We will compare the working of a basic income to other types of government transfers in cash and in kind, and analyse their potential to reduce income inequality. We will contrast the experimental design and most important results of the Basic Income Pilot Project to an earlier trial carried out in Finland in 2017–18. And we will survey the structure of the German taxation system and assess the feasibility of funding a basic income. Is this course for me? This course is open to all students. There are no prerequisites. Workload and assessment: Students will qualify for 5 ECTS points if their attendance is satisfactory, they engage with the course materials, including a reading of some 20 pages each week, and they pass the examination. courses.title: The Politics of German Coal
courses.description: Kommentar: Subject: This year somewhat more than one-fifth of the electricity generated in Germany will come from burning a type of (soft) coal called lignite, and those coal-fired power stations will account for approximately 30 per cent of German CO2 emissions due to the combustion of fossil fuels. To reduce those emissions the federal government under chan¬cellor Merkel legislated to phase out coal power by 2038, while the next government—a coalition of Social Demo¬cratic, Green and Free Democratic parties—had agreed to bring that date forward to 2030. Then Russia invaded Ukraine, and now the “end of coal” in Germany seems to be in jeopardy. Program: To gain some perspective on German coal politics today, we will trace the remarkable persistence of coal as a major political theme through¬out German history. We will survey the development and importance of coal during each of the German political regimes, focusing on the DDR in particular. We will contrast the economic, (geo)political and other social circumstances of the current phase-out of coal power to the previous phase-outs of (hard) coal and nuclear power, which were completed in 2018 and 2023 respectively. We will also compare the economics and (geo)politics of lignite versus natural gas. The seminar will include an intro¬duction to the carbon cycle and global warming for students without a background in the sciences. Is this course for me? This course is open to all students. There are no prerequisites. Workload and assessment: Students will qualify for 5 ECTS points if their attendance is satisfactory, they engage with the course materials, including a reading of some 20 pages each week, and they pass the examination. courses.title: Citizenship and Integration in Germany
courses.description: Kommentar: Subject: A major reform of German citizenship law took effect in mid 2024, which made it simpler for immigrants and their descendants to become German citizens. According to the government the reform was intended to promote integration. Arguably it is the most prominent component of an integration policy developed by German governments since the turn of the century. Program: We will take the changes to citizenship law as the starting point for an analysis of integration in Germany. We will consider the definition of integration with regard to work and language, and also in education, drawing in particular on the results of the PISA study. We will debate the meaning of cultural integration, especially with regard to religion, and compare it to concepts like assimilation and multiculturalism. And we will set the idea of integration in historical perspective, tracing its development in connection to geopolitics and immigration since the end of war in 1945. Is this course for me? This course is open to all students. There are no prerequisites. Workload and assessment: Students will qualify for 5 ECTS points if their attendance is satisfactory, they engage with the course materials, including a reading of some 20 pages each week, and they pass the examination. courses.title: Reading Hitler: (auto)biography as history
courses.description: Kommentar: Subject: Ian Kershaw argued that the legacy of Adolf Hitler “belongs to us all,” and that “part of that legacy is the continuing duty to seek understanding of how Hitler was possible.” For that purpose Kershaw saw biography as indispensable. But he warned that biography “runs the natural risk of over-personalizing complex historical developments, [and] over-emphasizing the role of the individual in shaping and determining events.” Biography, then, poses dilemmas which arise whenever we seek to understand human affairs, past or present. Program: We will draw on several biographies of Hitler and of those close to him to study important episodes in his personal and political career. We will read about his childhood, his experience of war and peace, and his accumulation of power, first in the Nazi party, then in the German parliament and government. We will consider his role in the drafting of the Nuremberg laws and in the diplomacy leading to the Munich agreement, and discuss the ways in which biographers have responded to the question of his personal responsibility for the war and for the holocaust. And we will see that even his death gave rise to a debate over the role of government in the dissemination of information, which reappeared in a different aspect when historians came to edit his autobiography, Mein Kampf, seventy years later. Is this course for me? This course is open to all students. There are no prerequisites. Workload and assessment: Students will qualify for 5 ECTS points if their attendance is satisfactory, they engage with the course materials, including a reading of some 20 pages each week, and they pass the examination. Schließen

courses.title: Das Interview als Textsorte und literarisches Verfahren
courses.description: Kommentar: Interviews sind in Zeitungen, im Radio, im Fernsehen, in Podcasts und in sozialen Medien seit längerem so präsent, dass man von einer „Interviewgesellschaft“ (Hoffmann/Kaiser) gesprochen hat. Auch im Literaturbetrieb kommt dem Interview als einer überaus wirksamen Form schriftstellerischer Selbstinszenierung zentrale Bedeutung zu. Nicht zuletzt finden sich Interviewstrukturen in literarischen Texten: fiktive Interviews, ganze Romane oder Teile davon in Interviewform. Wo aber verläuft die Grenze zwischen protokollierter Rede und literarischer Gestaltung, zwischen Dokumentation und Fiktion? Wie verändern Verschriftlichung, Redaktion und Publikationskontext die Form des Gesagten? Ist es möglich, zwischen journalistischen Interviews, literarischen Interviews, gefälschten Interviews, fiktiven Interviews und Interviewromanen zu unterscheiden? Welche ästhetischen Effekte entstehen, wenn das Interview in literarische Texte eingeht oder diese strukturiert? Welche Rolle spielen die für das Interview charakteristische Spannung zwischen Mündlichkeit und Schriftlichkeit und die doppelte oder mehrfache Autorschaft im je konkreten Fall? Diese und ähnliche Fragen werden wir im Seminar diskutieren. Grundlage sind Autor:inneninterviews und Interviewtexte (bzw. Auszüge) von/mit John von Düffel, Wolf Haas, Elfriede Jelinek, Brigitte Kronauer, Tom Kummer, André Müller, Kathrin Röggla, Clemens J. Setz, Ben Witter u.a. Zur Einführung empfohlen: Torsten Hoffmann: Interviews. Zur Inszenierung von Nicht-Inszeniertheit, in: Literatur fu¨r Leser 38/2 (2015), Sonderheft: Literaturbetriebspraktiken, S. 99–111. Klaus Birnstiel: Interview, Präsenz, Paratext. Versuch einer vorläufigen Feldbestimmung, in: Torsten Hoffmann/Gerhard Kaiser (Hrsg.): Echt inszeniert. Interviews in Literatur und Literaturbetrieb, Paderborn 2014, S. 63–80. Torsten Hoffmann/Gerhard Kaiser: Echt inszeniert. Schriftstellerinterviews als Forschungsgegenstand, in: dies. (Hrsg.): Echt inszeniert. Interviews in Literatur und Literaturbetrieb, Paderborn 2014, S. 9-25. Schließen

courses.title: Propaganda: Concept and History
courses.description:
Hinweise für Studierende: Ab dem 20.10.26 findet das Seminar im Raum KL 29/111 statt!

Kommentar: Topic: Most people think of sinister things when they hear the word ‘propaganda’: What comes to mind is probably the National Socialist “Minister for Public Enlightenment and Propaganda”, Dr. Joseph Goebbels, and NS propaganda more generally in film, visual arts, mass media and architecture, or perhaps the malicious propaganda devices depicted in George Orwell’s dystopian novel 1984 such as psychological manipulation used to control people’s minds and speech through “newspeak” and “doublethink”, disinformation and hate campaigns, and the constant re-writing and re-interpretation of history. However, this view is neither accurate nor helpful when it comes to understanding and critically evaluating propaganda. Propaganda is not limited to authoritarian governments, nor is it predominantly used by the state, and it may even serve beneficial purposes. In fact, propaganda is much more ubiquitous that many people realise, which makes it even more relevant to understand what it means and how it works. Historical examples will help, but propaganda is in no way a merely historical phenomenon. Program: The course will consist of three main parts: Firstly, we will define propaganda and discuss the differences between propaganda on the one hand and persuasion, disinformation, manipulation or fake news on the other hand. In the second part, we will examine specific examples from (German) history, such as German and anti-German propaganda during World War I, NS propaganda, and socialist propaganda in the GDR. And in the final part, we will discuss more recent campaigns, discussing whether or to what extent they can be seen as propaganda. Is this the right course for you? The course is open to students from all fields, from the sciences as well as from the humanities. However, you should be able to read complex English texts, be prepared to study a wide variety of theoretical as well as literary texts and be interested in the topic as well as in in-depth analysis of texts and films. Workload and Assessment: To obtain 5 ECTS credits, you will have to study and engage with the course materials (an average of 15-20 pages of academic texts per week), pass a mid-term test before Christmas and sit a written exam at the end of the semester. If you want to participate, you must attend the first, at the latest the second session. Students must attend at least 85% of the classes (14 out of 16). Some of the materials will be available in digital form on Blackboard; additionally, students have to purchase the reader (a collection of photocopied texts in printed form) from the copy shop at Königin-Luise-Str. 39, near U-Bahnhof Dahlem Dorf. courses.title: Humans and Animals: A Complex Relationship in Literature (and Film)
courses.description: Kommentar: Topic: Humans have hunted, killed, and eaten other mammals for more than 2 million years. We see animals in prehistoric cave paintings, and they play crucial roles in myths and legends of ancient cultures. For thousands of years, humans have reared mammals and birds for food and utilised the physical strength of horses and oxen for work. Some animals are bred and kept as pets, put on display in zoos and trained as circus attractions. Other animals are regarded as pests or predators which must be controlled or exterminated. Human history is in fact inconceivable without (non-human) animals. But while animals have played a role in the life sciences for a long time, cultural animal studies are a relatively new phenomenon. This course will serve as an introduction to this field. Program: We will study academic and literary texts from the 19th and 20th centuries and examine some of the most relevant ways in which humans have related to animals, perceiving or using them as prey, livestock, food, predators, or pests, and exploring similarities and differences between humans and non-human animals. Most of the texts were written by British, Canadian or US-American authors, one – a text by Franz Kafka – was originally written in German and translated into English; additionally, we will discuss Werner Herzog’s American documentary film Grizzly Man. Trigger Warning: Some of the texts contain features which sensitive students may find hard to process – such as detailed descriptions of hunting, slaughter, and other forms of killing animals (and humans). Is this the right course for you? The course is open to students from all fields, from the sciences as well as from the humanities. However, you should be able to read complex English texts, be prepared to study a wide variety of theoretical as well as literary texts and be interested in the topic as well as in in-depth analysis of texts and films. courses.title: Creative Writing
courses.description: Kommentar: Topic: Living and studying in a foreign country can be an exciting time in your personal and intellectual development. One productive way of dealing with the onslaught of impressions is to write about it. This course is designed to help you transform your ideas into a well-considered piece of literary writing. The resulting text may be fictional or non-fictional. It could take the form of a short story set in Berlin, a literary reportage, a creative essay, a series of poems or even the beginning chapter of a novel. Program: This course will be conducted workshop-style. You will work on your own writing project throughout the semester and share and discuss it with your fellow students and the instructor. In addition, we will conduct short writing exercises and discuss assigned texts about the process of writing. Can I take this course? Yes – if you are interested in literature and wish to try your hand at creative writing. You should be open-minded toward your fellow students, and willing to share and discuss your work with them. You should be prepared to accept and dispense constructive criticism, and to establish a regular daily writing practice: a few minutes of notetaking after breakfast or half an hour of writing before you go to sleep. Your English may not be perfect, but you are willing to own your mistakes and work on your grammar, vocabulary, and style. Requirements and Grading: In order to earn 5 ECTS credits you will have to attend at least 80 percent of scheduled sessions. The instructor reserves the right to refuse admission after the second week of the semester. Course participants will engage with the reading materials and respond to a selection of them; post all writing assignments by the indicated due dates; respond to their fellow students' work online and in discussion. The final writing project, due on the last day of class, will be about ten pages in length. Schließen

courses.title: Technopoly: Being Human in the Age of Digitalisation and AI
courses.description: Kommentar: Topic: "Artificial intelligence will reshape the material conditions of human life on a scale that no technology has accomplished since the harnessing of electricity, and perhaps beyond even that." Such are the predictions of Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI which launched the first public version of ChatGPT in 2022. Ever since then, tech leaders, developers, experts from different fields, and users exchange views on the potential social, economic, environmental, educational, cultural, and political impact of AI. Some see a future without work and with a bounty of wealth, a world in which AI will solve all of humanity’s problems such as climate change, inequality, or hunger, and in which every person might benefit from personalised AI tutors, AI doctors, AI companions and robot nurses or surgeons. Others fear that AI will lead to a dystopian future imagined in Science Fiction movies such as The Terminator in which the fictional artificial general superintelligence system SkyNet is set on the extermination of humans. Between these extreme positions, debates focus on AI’s more immediate impact on work, academia, use of resources, publishing, art, and political communication. But beyond the immediate impact: What does Sam Altman’s statement imply? How might AI change human life? And what does it mean to be human, if there is a new technology that may be better at most of the things that up to now have made us, in our view, unique? Program: Based on (mostly recent) academic and journalistic texts, we will explore some of the key aspects in the larger-scale visions regarding the utopian and dystopian dimensions of AI. The course will focus on three skills that are considered crucial for successful studying: reading (and understanding) texts, writing, and discussing complex issues. Ironically, reading and writing in particular are increasingly outsources to AI; not just in universities, but also in politics and journalism. In this course, students will have the opportunity for an open debate about these complex issues. Is this the right course for you? Apart from having a fundamental interest in the topic, students should be prepared to participate in debates about controversial topics and to examine, explore, and question their own use of AI. You should be prepared to participate in class discussions and group work. Workload and assessment: For the 5 ECTS credits, students have to attend classes, study course materials (academic and non-academic texts as well as some videos/ podcasts) and produce written and oral statements in class. The final exam will be an oral examination of ca. 10-15 minutes. Schließen

Die Teilnehmenden reflektieren Merkmale des wissenschaftlichen Stils, erproben Werkzeuge zur Textproduktion und -überarbeitung, lernen den verantwortungsvollen und kritischen Einsatz von KI-Tools kennen und die typischen „Do’s and Don’ts“ beim akademischen Schreiben. courses.title: Theorie, Methode und Geschichte der Geschichtswissenschaft
courses.description: Kommentar: „Geschichte studieren… was heißt das eigentlich? Dieses Seminar bietet Ihnen eine allgemeine Einführung in die Geschichtswissenschaft und führt in die Praxis des wissenschaftlichen Arbeitens ein. In Anlehnung an die Vorlesung werden verschiedene Ansätze der Geschichtswissenschaften aufgegriffen und relevante Fähigkeiten für das Studium vermittelt. Ausgehend vom thematischen Schwerpunkt “Deutsche Kolonialgeschichte” werden die grundlegenden Kompetenzen für ein erfolgreiches Geschichtsstudium vermittelt: Dazu zählen das Auffinden, gezielte Lesen und Zitieren von geeigneter Forschungsliteratur, der (kritische) Umgang mit Quellen, das Entwickeln einer wissenschaftlichen Fragestellung sowie die Konzeption einer Hausarbeit. Es werden Fragen beantwortet wie: Wie lese, bearbeite und verstehe ich einen wissenschaftlichen Text? Wie bibliographiere ich richtig? Was ist eine Quelle und wie interpretiere ich sie? Wie formuliere ich eine wissenschaftliche Fragestellung? Wie verfasse ich ein Exposé und eine Hausarbeit? Schritt für Schritt werden im Seminar Techniken des wissenschaftlichen Arbeitens vorgestellt. Die aktive Mitarbeit besteht aus wöchentlichen Übungen und schriftlichen Abgaben. Die Bereitschaft zu englischer Lektüre, zur aktiven Mitarbeit sowie zu regelmäßiger Gruppenarbeit wird unbedingt vorausgesetzt. Den Modulabschluss bildet eine Hausarbeit.“ Schließen

courses.title: Der Zweite Weltkrieg: Eine globale Perspektive
courses.description: Kommentar: Am Beispiel des Zweiten Weltkrieges beschäftigt sich das Seminar mit der Entstehung von extremer Gewalt und den Auswirkungen, die diese auf Gesellschaften und Staaten, soziale Gemeinschaften und Individuen hat. Welche neuen Fragen und Erkenntnisse lassen sich gewinnen, wenn wir den Zweiten Weltkrieg aus globaler Perspektive (vergleichend, transregional oder transnational) betrachten, und dabei sowohl makro- als auch mikrogeschichtliche Ansätze verbinden? Das Seminar ist thematisch strukturiert und beschäftigt sich u.a. mit Fragen von Ideologie, extremer Gewalt und Brutalisierung; Okkupation, Kollaboration und Widerstand; Partisanenkrieg und Zivilbevölkerung; und Geschlecht und Gewalt. Beginnend in den späten 1930er Jahren liegt der Fokus des Seminars auf den Hauptkriegsschauplätzen in Europa und Asien. Das Seminar endet in der Nachkriegszeit und fragt nach der Bedeutung von Strafrechtsprozessen, Erinnerung und Vergangenheitspolitik. Als Teil eines Feldforschungsprojekts werden sich die Studierenden zudem (mithilfe von Fotokameras) im Berliner Stadtraum und Umland auf die Suche nach den visuellen Spuren des Zweiten Weltkriegs machen – ob groß oder klein, sichtbar oder verdeckt. Bitte beachten Sie, dass ein Großteil der Forschungsliteratur englischsprachig ist. Schließen

courses.title: Multiethnisches Leben in urbanen Zentren Ostmitteleuropas, 1860-1914
courses.description:
Kommentar: Ostmitteleuropäische Metropolen und Kleinstädte wurden bis zum Ersten Weltkrieg und teilweise auch bis zur Schoah von zwei, drei oder mehr ethnischen Gruppen bewohnt. Das Zusammenleben brachte verschiedene Formen multikultureller Interaktionen und Umgangsformen hervor, die den Alltag strukturierten und das berufliche Leben prägten. Das Leben in multiethnischen Städten war sowohl von langen Phasen friedlicher Koexistenz als auch wirtschaftlichen, politischen und kulturellen Konflikten gekennzeichnet. In diesem Seminar untersuchen wir anhand konkreter Beispiele, wie multiethnische Städte in Ostmitteleuropa auf der kommunalen, staatlichen und imperialen Ebene verwaltet wurden, wie die Koexistenz verschiedener ethnischer Gruppen verlief, welche kulturellen und politischen Formen des Zusammenlebens entstanden und wie ethnische Konflikte im urbanen Raum geschürt und ausgetragen wurden. Schließen

Literaturhinweise: Moritz Csáky, Das Gedächtnis der Städte. Kulturelle Verflechtungen - Wien und die urbanen Milieus in Zentraleuropa, Köln 2010; Friedrich Langer, Metropolen der Moderne: Eine europäische Stadtgeschichte seit 1850, München 2013; Michael F. Hamm (Hrsg.), The City in Late Imperial Russia, Bloomington 1986; Omer Bartov / Eric Weitz, Shatterzone of Empires. Coexistence and Violence in the German, Habsburg, Russian, and Ottoman Borderlands, Bloomington 2013; Ulrich Hofmeister/ Florian Riedler, Imperial Cities in the Tsarist, the Habsburg, and the Ottoman Empires, London 2024; Catherine Horel, Multicultural Cities of the Habsburg Empire, 1880-1914 Imagined Communities and Conflictual Encounters, New York 2023. Schließen

courses.description: Kommentar: In this hands-on course, participants carry out their own research projects on the topic of "Representations of East Asia, Representations of the Self in Social Media" and learn how to design and execute their own research projects, exploring how East Asia is represented and how individuals from East Asia present themselves on digital platforms. Students will reflect on methodological issues through the lens of their individual projects, enhancing their ability to adapt and refine their approach. Proficiency in one East Asian language is required, ensuring that participants can engage with primary sources and conduct interviews effectively. Schließen

Anhand der gemeinsamen Lektüre von Texten werden verschiedene Zugänge des zwanzigsten Jahrhunderts zur Geschichtswissenschaft erörtert. Zudem bietet das Seminar eine praxisorientierte Einführung in die Werkzeuge und Techniken (geschichts-)wissenschaftlichen Arbeitens wie Literaturrecherche, Quelleninterpretation, relevante Internet-Angebote und das Verfassen schriftlicher Arbeiten. Eine hohe Bereitschaft zur Lektüre deutsch- und englischsprachiger Fachliteratur sowie zum Verfassen eigener wissenschaftlicher Texte wird vorausgesetzt. Schließen

courses.title: (S) VM: SoWi "Gender and politics in contemporary Japan"
courses.description:
Hinweise für Studierende: Dieser Kurs findet auf Englisch statt.

Kommentar: Despite its status as an established democracy, Japan has long ranked comparatively low on major international indices of gender equality, particularly with regard to women’s political representation and socio-economic empowerment. Its record on the representation and protection of sexual minorities has likewise been limited. Against this background, the course addresses questions such as: What factors contribute to gender inequality in Japan? What measures have been taken to address these inequalities? And how do individual actors participate in politics and seek to represent the interests of women and sexual minorities in civil society and public office? To explore these questions, the seminar first provides an overview of theoretical and empirical research on gender politics. It then examines the gendered consequences of Japan’s political, legal, and socio-economic institutions, including the electoral system, the household registration, and the gendered division of labour. Finally, the course discusses how women shape politics both within and beyond established political institutions and evaluates Japanese government policies alongside international examples of affirmative action. In addition to the substantive focus on gender politics, the module engages original Japanese-language sources and covers the fundamentals of academic writing and research methods, equipping participants with the tools needed to conduct independent research. Schließen

courses.title: (S) VM: SoWi "Whose voice matters? Representation and exclusion in Japanese politics and society"
courses.description:
Hinweise für Studierende: Dieser Kurs findet auf Englisch statt.

Kommentar: Contemporary democracies are built on the ideal of political representation: elected officials are expected to reflect the voices of the people in decision-making and to be held accountable when they fail to do so. But whose voices are heard, and whose are left out? And who gets to represent them? This module explores these questions through the lens of Japan—one of Asia’s oldest democracies and a particularly intriguing case, marked by long-term one-party dominance, weak opposition and social movements, as well as persistent social inequalities. These features underscore the importance of a closer evaluation of how inclusive Japan’s representative system truly is. The module provides a critical overview of major theoretical debates and empirical research on the relationship between citizens and their representatives in Japan. It will specifically examine how electoral rules, legal structures, and social norms shape the political elites, their responsiveness to the interests of the citizens and the resultant patterns of exclusion, for instance, along ideological, economic, regional, or gender lines. It will further investigate the extent to which non-state actors, such as social movements and media, influence representation processes in Japan. Finally, the module will engage Japanese sources to deepen the understanding of these issues and hone academic writing and research skills, equipping course participants with a toolset for independent research. Schließen

courses.title: VS-Colonial and Postcolonial Literatures: Writing South Africa
courses.description: Kommentar: South Africa is a county marked by a troubled history of extreme violence and economic strength – a history that saw the colonisation by various European countries, enslavement, the destruction of indigeneity, apartheid, a new start as the rainbow nation and today’s battles against inequality, xenophobia, homophobia and economic decline. This complex intersection of historical legacies has not only affected South African politics of decolonisation but has also left its mark on the literature of the nation. It has generated many experimental texts that cover a wide range of perspectives from the legacies of colonisation to the effects of globalisation. In this seminar we will look at poetry, short stories and novels by (among others) J.M Coetzee, Zakes Mda, Nadine Gordimer, and Phaswane Mpe. Schließen
