courses.title: Welt-Bilder: Bildanalyse und visuelle Kommunikation in der Konfliktforschung
courses.description: Kommentar: Wir leben im Zeitalter der bildbasierten Kommunikation. Auch unsere Wahrnehmung von politischen Konflikten wird stark durch ihre visuelle und mediale Darstellung geprägt. Politik zeigt sich in den Bildern, die uns täglich umgeben – von den sozialen Medien über die traditionellen Nachrichten bis hin zu Demoschildern oder Werbung auf der Straße. Während sich die meisten Ansätze der Friedens- und Konfliktforschung nur auf Textmaterial konzentrieren, erschließt die Bildanalyse auch visuelle Quellen, um Konflikte systematisch zu untersuchen. Das Seminar führt zunächst theoretisch in Basisliteratur der Visual Culture (Bildwissenschaften) ein, um anschließend methodische Zugänge der Bildanalyse vorzustellen und praktisch auszutesten. Es dient den Studierenden zur ersten Reflexion darüber, wie Bilder in der Politik eingesetzt werden und in der Friedens- und Konfliktforschung zum Verständnis von Konflikten beitragen können. Schließen

courses.title: Neuroscience Across Biophysical Scales
courses.description:
Zusätzl. Angaben / Voraussetzungen: Rooms: 22.10. - 19.11.2026 HS Kristallographie (Takustr. 6) 25.11.2026 - 11.02.2027 Cohn-Hörsaal (Virchowweg 24, 10117 Berlin-Mitte)

Kommentar: 22.10.2026 Towards a mechanistic understanding of instinctive behaviours, Vanessa Stempel In this lecture, I will give a brief overview of the history of the field of (neuro-)ethology and the study of instinctive behaviours– including defence, hunting and parental care. This set of behaviours has evolved across animal phyla to ensure survival with ‘pre-wired’ circuits, but the expression of these behaviours is flexible, by changing with the environmental context, past experiences, and needs of the animal to ensure survival. I will present recent and ongoing work in my lab that aims to mechanistically understand how the brain generates instinctive behaviours. In particular, I will focus on mammalian brainstem circuits that control the production of virtually all instinctive behaviours, and discuss their implementation across scales-from synapses to circuits to behaviour. 29.10.2026 Sleep, synaptic plasticity and brain resilience, Stephan Sigrist How does the brain maintain function while adapting to experience, metabolic state and aging? I will discuss our work on presynaptic active-zone remodeling and its links to sleep, memory and neuronal resilience, and emerging evidence that metabolic interventions can influence these adaptive brain states. 19.11.2026 Microglia - guardians of the brain shaping neural function in health and disease, Christian Madry This talk will provide an overview of our research exploring the versatile roles of microglia, the brain's innate immune cells, under physiological and pathological conditions. After introducing this fascinating and highly dynamic glial cell type, I will first highlight our discoveries of the cellular and molecular mechanisms governing microglial morphodynamics and surveillance of the brain parenchyma. I will then demonstrate that microglial surveillance serves functions far beyond monitoring the brain environment: guided by neuronal activity, microglia engage in neuroimmune feedback mechanisms that shape neuronal network dynamics and maintain brain homeostasis. Finally, I will turn to the pathophysiological roles of microglia, focusing on our current research into the molecular mechanisms underlying microglial contributions to neuroinflammation and Alzheimer's disease. 25.11.2026 The processing of memories in the hippocampus, Dietmar Schmitz One of the most captivating questions in neuroscience revolves around the brain's ability to efficiently and durably capture and store information. It must process continuous input from sensory organs while also encoding memories that can persist throughout a lifetime. What are the cellular, subcellular, and network-level mechanisms that underlie this remarkable capacity for long-term information storage? As the hippocampus plays a pivotal role in memory, our lecture focuses on three aspects: 1) brief introduction in the so-called ‚synaptic-plasticity-memory-hypothesis‘, 2) two-stage model of memory consolidation, 3) high-frequency oscillations: circuit-diagrams & propagation of sharp-wave-ripples We explore how these three elements shape the processing of memories in the hippocampus. 10.12.2026 Stress, Resilience, and Depression: Insights from rodent models, Hanna Hörnberg I will discuss how rodent models can provide insights into the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying stress susceptibility and resilience, with a particular focus on combining advanced behavioral phenotyping with brain region- and cell type-specific omics approaches. 17.12.2026 The extraordinary neurobiology of the naked mole-rat, Gary Lewin I will discuss how the social structure of naked mole-rat colonies is controlled. I will put this into the context of the unique neurobiology of this species which lives in highly cooperative colonies that can efficiently exploit a harsh environment. 07.01.2027 Large Brain Neuroscience in Elephants, Michael Brecht Most of cellular neuroscience focuses on small brains (worms, flies & mice). I present data on structure and function of the large elephant brain. Elephant brains differ markedly from smaller brains in subcellular, cellular and network structure. I will discuss approaches for elucidating elephant brain structure and relating it to elephant cognition and sleep 14.01.2027 Neural circuits and behavior in sleep and camouflage, Gilles Laurent Using our recent experimental work on cephalopod camouflage and on reptilian sleep as examples, I will try and illustrate the importance of combining not only technical approaches, but also perspectives (computational, evolutionary etc), to understand the designs and operations of brains. 21.01.2027 Neuronal circuits of thermal perception, James Poulet The thermosensory system plays a fundamental role in shaping somatosensory perception, regulating core body physiology and protecting organisms from environmental harm. Compared with other sensory systems, the neural circuits underlying thermal perception are less understood. However, recent advances have provided insights into the wiring of the thermosensory pathways, cellular principles of thermal encoding, and their relationship to perception. Traditionally regarded as a relatively slow and modulatory sense, it is now recognized as a fast, highly sensitive sensory system capable of complex computations including multisensory integration and the generation of sensory illusions. Here I discuss recent progress in the understanding of the neural mechanisms of innocuous thermal processing and perception. Intriguingly, although warm and cool reflect opposite changes along the same physical dimension, they differ markedly in both their perception and encoding in the nervous system. I argue that the thermal system is an excellent model to advance our understanding of the neural mechanisms of sensory perception and sensory guided behaviours. 09.02.2027 The Parallel Evolution of Complex Cognition, Onur Güntürkün Great apes such as chimpanzees have complex cognitive abilities and a brain weighing approximately 400 g, which includes a large neocortex. In comparison, birds such as corvids and parrots have a brain weighing between 3 and 25 g and no neocortex. How then it is possible that there is not a single cognitive ability in chimpanzees that has not also been demonstrated to the same level in corvids and parrots? This question keeps me awake at night because it challenges fundamental assumptions about the neural basis of complex cognition. This talk is about this question. Schließen

courses.title: Einführung in die Theorie und Ästhetik
(HS) Sexuelle Ökonomien
courses.description: Kommentar: Dieses Seminar beschäftigt sich mit den vielfältigen Verflechtungen von Sexualität, Intimität und Ökonomie und ihrer Analyse aus kultur- und sozialanthropologischer Perspektive. Einführend werden wir uns den Begriffen ‘Sexarbeit’, ‘Prostitution’ und ‘transactional sex’ kritisch annähern und die Problematik der Definition sexueller Ökonomien und damit verbundener hegemonialer (Sexual-)Normen analysieren. Anschließend werden wir anhand ethnographischer Beispiele lokale Praktiken und Deutungen transaktionaler sexueller Handlungen diskutieren und Zusammenhänge mit Geschlechterverhältnissen, Arbeitsmärkten, Moralvorstellungen und verschiedenen Formen von Marginalisierung herausarbeiten. Diese Beispiele werden in Folge in breiteren Kontexten verortet, um die Verflechtungen sexueller Ökonomien mit u.a. (Arbeits-)Migration, globalen Ungleichverhältnissen und struktureller Diskriminierung zu veranschaulichen. Schließlich diskutieren wir auch darüber, welche Rolle(n) Forschung in diesem Feld einnehmen kann und wie sich Forschende diesem vorurteilsbelasteten Thema kritisch anthropologisch annähern können. Schließen
